description: Eleven free Claude skills that clone any app: reverse-engineer it, rebuild it, test it for bugs, then fix what its users hate. Free, MIT.

summary.one_liner: A set of eleven free Claude skills that reverse-engineer an app's features and flows, rebuild them clean-room, test, compare and rebrand the clone, and then fix the complaints users have about the original.
keywords: build my own version of an app
use_cases: Map an existing web or mobile app's screens, flows and data model before cloning it
Plan the stack, database schema and API for a clone
Turn screenshots into design tokens and check colour contrast
Test a rebuilt app's flows for bugs with Playwright specs
Score a clone's feature parity against the original
Find recurring user complaints in reviews and draft a positioning angle
stack: Next.js, Postgres, Stripe, Resend (suggested by the architect skill for the example)
notable: Eleven skills run in sequence from recon to deploy, each reading the previous skill's output in a replica/ folder
Entrepreneur skill only uses reviews with links and reports sample sizes; reviews.py drops any review without a URL
parity.py weights must/should/could features and never scores items left out on purpose
sweep.py scans the codebase for the original app's name, domain and colours and blocks deploy until clean
imgdiff.py compares screenshot layouts using edge maps so colour changes do not count against the clone
caveats: Explicitly rebuilds features and flows only, not the original's code, logos, copy, content or network; the author says it is not legal advice and recommends trademark checks and a lawyer before selling
No guarantee of a perfect clone; complexity varies (README gives a booking tool as weeks of work and a spreadsheet engine as out of reach)
Can only read public pages and the user's own account; the README says it will not scrape behind logins or past paywalls
